skills.name: benchmarking
skills.description: Guide for building, running, and analyzing Nanvix performance benchmarks. Use this when asked about benchmark setup, execution, or interpretation.

skills.name: build
skills.description: Guide for building, formatting, linting, and spell-checking Nanvix with z. Use this when asked to build or validate the repository.

skills.name: ci-cd-pipeline
skills.description: Guide for Nanvix CI and GitHub Actions workflow behavior, including local pipeline execution and matrix coverage. Use this when asked about CI checks, workflow failures, or release flow.

skills.name: coding-standards
skills.description: Detailed Nanvix coding, documentation, and review standards across Rust, C/C++, Python, and Shell. Use this when asked to implement or review code quality conventions.

skills.name: daemon-development
skills.description: Guide for developing and debugging Nanvix daemons, including guest daemons and host linuxd behavior. Use this when asked about daemon architecture or daemon changes.

skills.name: gdb-debugging
skills.description: Guide for debugging Nanvix guests using GDB remote debugging over the microvm machine type. Use this when asked about attaching GDB, setting breakpoints, or stepping through kernel code.

skills.name: kernel-development
skills.description: Guide for modifying and debugging the Nanvix kernel architecture and kernel-call paths. Use this when asked about kernel internals or kernel implementation changes.

skills.name: library-development
skills.description: Guide for creating and modifying Nanvix libraries under src/libs, including guest no_std and host std crates. Use this when asked about library architecture or crate changes.

skills.name: test-development
skills.description: Guide for writing, running, and debugging Nanvix unit, integration, and system tests in Rust and C/C++. Use this when asked about test implementation or failures.

skills.name: test
skills.description: Guide for running Nanvix tests with z. Use this when asked to run unit tests, integration tests, or the full test suite.

skills.name: troubleshooting
skills.description: Guide for diagnosing Nanvix build, runtime, and test failures, including cleanup and debugging workflows. Use this when asked to investigate errors or unstable behavior.

skills.name: user-app-development
skills.description: Guide for developing, building, and running Nanvix user-space applications across supported runtimes and languages. Use this when asked about guest app implementation or execution.

skills.name: find-skills
skills.description: Helps users discover and install agent skills when they ask questions like "how do I do X", "find a skill for X", "is there a skill that can...", or express interest in extending capabilities. This skill should be used when the user is looking for functionality that might exist as an installable skill.

skills.name: customize-cloud-agent
skills.description: Skill for customizing the Copilot cloud agent (formerly known as Copilot coding agent) environment, including copilot-setup-steps.yml configuration, preinstalling tools and dependencies, runners, and settings. Use when the user mentions copilot-setup-steps, copilot setup steps, or wants to configure the cloud agent environment.

1. // Copyright(c) The Maintainers of Nanvix.
2. // Licensed under the MIT License.
3. 
4. //==================================================================================================
5. // Modules
6. //==================================================================================================
7. 
8. use vstd::prelude::*;
9. 
10. pub(crate) mod frame;
11. mod kframe;
12. mod manager;
13. mod upool;
14. 
15. #[cfg(feature = "test")]
16. mod test;
17. 
18. //==================================================================================================
19. // Imports
20. //==================================================================================================
21. 
22. use crate::{
23.     hal::mem::{
24.         Address,
25.         PageAligned,
26.         PhysicalAddress,
27.         TruncatedMemoryRegion,
28.         VirtualAddress,
29.     },
30.     mm::phys::upool::Upool,
31. };
32. use ::alloc::collections::LinkedList;
33. use ::arch::mem;
34. use ::bitmap::Bitmap;
35. use ::sys::error::Error;
36. #[cfg(verus_keep_ghost)]
37. use ::vstd::prelude::*;
38. 
39. // Include specifications.
40. #[cfg(verus_keep_ghost)]
41. include!("mod.spec.rs");
42. #[cfg(verus_keep_ghost)]
43. include!("mod.proof.rs");
44. 
45. //==================================================================================================
46. // Exports
47. //==================================================================================================
48. 
49. pub use self::{
50.     kframe::KernelFrame,
51.     manager::PhysMemoryManager,
52.     upool::UserFrame,
53. };
54. 
55. //==================================================================================================
56. // Standalone Functions
57. //==================================================================================================
58. 
59. // This function iterates the supplied `LinkedList` of regions. The std `LinkedList`
60. // iterator cannot be given a Verus `for`-loop specification from this crate (the orphan
61. // rule forbids implementing vstd's iterator traits for the foreign `Iter` type, and the
62. // pinned `vstd` dependency cannot be extended — see `mod.spec.rs` / `verus-unsupported.md`).
63. // The function is therefore `external_body`; its `#[verus_spec]` contract is honored by the
64. // caller (`init`). The abstract effect — every frame of every region becomes booked — is
65. // modelled by `PhysMemView::spec_book_frames` / `region_frames` and discharged by
66. // `lemma_book_region_reserves_region_frames` in `mod.proof.rs`. Because the region frames are
67. // the contents of the (un-viewable) `LinkedList`, they cannot be enumerated in this boundary
68. // contract; what is expressed is the caller-relevant guarantee that the allocator stays
69. // initialized and well-formed across booking.
70. #[verus_verify(external_body)]
71. #[verus_spec(result =>
72.     requires
73.         phys_view().initialized,
74.         phys_view().inv(),
75.     ensures
76.         phys_view().inv(),
77.         match result {
78.             Ok(()) => phys_view().initialized,
79.             Err(_) => true,
80.         },
81. )]
82. fn book_physical_memory_regions(
83.     physical_memory_regions: LinkedList<TruncatedMemoryRegion<PhysicalAddress>>,
84. ) -> Result<(), Error> {
85.     info!("booking physical memory regions ...");
86. 
87.     // Book physical memory that is not usable.
88.     for region in physical_memory_regions.iter() {
89.         info!("booking: {:?}", region);
90.         frame::alloc_range(region)?;
91.     }
92. 
93.     Ok(())
94. }
95. 
96. // `external_body` for the same std-`LinkedList` reason as
97. // `book_physical_memory_regions`; its `#[verus_spec]` contract is honored by the caller
98. // (`init`). The abstract effect — every *tracked* MMIO frame (`is_covered`) becomes booked
99. // while untracked frames are skipped — is modelled by `PhysMemView::spec_book_frames` over
100. // `M.intersect(covered())` and discharged by `lemma_book_mmio_skip_untracked` /
101. // `lemma_book_mmio_books_tracked` in `mod.proof.rs`. As with the physical-region helper, the
102. // concrete MMIO frame set is the contents of the (un-viewable) `LinkedList`, so the boundary
103. // contract expresses the caller-relevant guarantee: the allocator stays initialized and
104. // well-formed (the skip-if-not-covered tolerance never aborts boot).
105. #[verus_verify(external_body)]
106. #[verus_spec(result =>
107.     requires
108.         phys_view().initialized,
109.         phys_view().inv(),
110.     ensures
111.         phys_view().inv(),
112.         match result {
113.             Ok(()) => phys_view().initialized,
114.             Err(_) => true,
115.         },
116. )]
117. fn book_mmio_regions(
118.     mmio_regions: &LinkedList<TruncatedMemoryRegion<VirtualAddress>>,
119. ) -> Result<(), Error> {
120.     info!("booking memory-mapped i/o regions ...");
121. 
122.     // Book memory-mapped I/O regions.
123.     for region in mmio_regions.iter() {
124.         info!("booking: {:?}", region);
125.         let mut start: usize = region.start().into_raw_value();
126.         let end: usize = start + (region.size() - 1);
127.         while start < end {
128.             let mmio_addr: usize = crate::hal::platform::gva_to_gpa(start);
129.             let phys_addr: PageAligned<PhysicalAddress> = PageAligned::from_address(unsafe {
130.                 // MMIO GPAs may legitimately lie outside tracked RAM, so they must not go through
131.                 // the regular physical-address validator here.
132.                 PhysicalAddress::from_mmio_address(VirtualAddress::from_raw_value(mmio_addr))?
133.             })?;
134. 
135.             // Only book frames that the frame allocator actually tracks.
136.             // MMIO regions above RAM (e.g. the LAPIC at 0xFEE0_0000) are not
137.             // covered by the bitmap and must be skipped.
138.             if frame::is_covered(phys_addr) {
139.                 frame::book(phys_addr)?;
140.             }
141.             start += mem::FRAME_SIZE;
142.         }
143.     }
144. 
145.     Ok(())
146. }
147. 
148. ///
149. /// # Description
150. ///
151. /// Initializes the physical memory manager.
152. ///
153. /// # Parameters
154. ///
155. /// - `physical_memory_regions`: Physical memory regions to book.
156. /// - `mmio_regions`: Memory-mapped I/O regions to book.
157. /// - `physical_memory_layout`: Physical memory layout bitmap.
158. ///
159. /// # Returns
160. ///
161. /// Upon success, `Ok(())` is returned. Upon failure, an error is returned instead.
162. ///
163. #[verus_spec(ret =>
164.     ensures
165.         // The frame-allocator invariant is established/preserved on every path: this
166.         // is the precondition every later `frame::*` / `PhysMemoryManager::*` call
167.         // relies on. (Vacuous before the allocator becomes initialized.)
168.         phys_view().inv(),
169.         match ret {
170.             // One-shot boot success: the global subsystem is now initialized and its
171.             // reservation state is well-formed, so reserved frames (allocated) are
172.             // disjoint from the free pool and can never be handed out by `alloc`.
173.             Ok(()) => {
174.                 &&& phys_view().initialized
175.                 &&& phys_view().frames.allocated_frames.disjoint(phys_view().frames.free_frames)
176.             },
177.             // Failure is terminal for the boot path; no completeness of reservation is
178.             // promised, only that the invariant still holds (checked above).
179.             Err(_) => true,
180.         },
181. )]
182. pub fn init(
183.     physical_memory_regions: LinkedList<TruncatedMemoryRegion<PhysicalAddress>>,
184.     mmio_regions: &LinkedList<TruncatedMemoryRegion<VirtualAddress>>,
185.     physical_memory_layout: Bitmap,
186. ) -> Result<(), Error> {
187.     // Initialize frame allocator singleton.
188.     info!("initializing the frame allocator ...");
189.     // Safety: called exactly once during single-threaded boot.
190.     unsafe { frame::init(physical_memory_layout)? };
191.     book_physical_memory_regions(physical_memory_regions)?;
192. 
193.     book_mmio_regions(mmio_regions)?;
194. 
195.     // Initialize user page pool.
196.     info!("initializing the user page pool ...");
197.     let upool: Upool = Upool::new();
198. 
199.     // Initialize physical memory manager singleton.
200.     info!("initializing the physical memory manager ...");
201.     PhysMemoryManager::init(upool)?;
202. 
203.     Ok(())
204. }
205. 
206. //==================================================================================================
207. // Standalone Functions
208. //==================================================================================================
209. 
210. #[cfg(feature = "test")]
211. pub fn test() -> bool {
212.     let mut passed = true;
213. 
214.     passed &= test::test();
215. 
216.     passed
217. }
218.

1. // Copyright(c) The Maintainers of Nanvix.
2. // Licensed under the MIT License.
3. 
4. // PhysMemoryManager - Specifications
5. //
6. // This file contains specification functions and view types.
7. 
8. verus! {
9. 
10. use crate::hal::mem::spec_page_size;
11. use vstd::map::*;
12. 
13. pub uninterp spec fn byte_at_address(ptr: int) -> u8;
14. 
15. /// Abstract view of the frame allocator (`frame::Inner`).
16. ///
17. /// Captures which physical frames are currently allocated vs. free,
18. /// together with a per-frame reference count that models shared
19. /// ownership (e.g. copy-on-write after `share()`).
20. pub struct FrameAllocView
21. {
22.     pub allocated_frames: Set<int>,
23.     pub free_frames: Set<int>,
24.     /// Maps each allocated frame address to its reference count.
25.     /// A frame is present in the map iff it is currently allocated.
26.     pub refcounts: Map<int, int>,
27. }
28. 
29. impl FrameAllocView
30. {
31.     pub open spec fn wf(&self) -> bool
32.     {
33.         // Page-alignment
34.         &&& forall|addr: int| self.allocated_frames.contains(addr) ==> addr % spec_page_size() == 0
35.         &&& forall|addr: int| self.free_frames.contains(addr) ==> addr % spec_page_size() == 0
36.         // Disjoint
37.         &&& self.allocated_frames.disjoint(self.free_frames)
38.         // Allocated ↔ refcount consistency: a frame is allocated iff it has a positive refcount
39.         &&& forall|addr: int| #[trigger] self.allocated_frames.contains(addr) <==>
40.             self.refcounts.contains_key(addr) && self.refcounts[addr] > 0
41.         // Free frames have no refcount entry
42.         &&& forall|addr: int| #[trigger] self.free_frames.contains(addr) ==>
43.             !self.refcounts.contains_key(addr)
44.         // Refcount bounded by u8 range
45.         &&& forall|addr: int| self.refcounts.contains_key(addr) ==>
46.             0 < self.refcounts[addr] <= 255
47.     }
48. }
49. 
50. } // end verus!
51. 
52. //==================================================================================================
53. // std `LinkedList` type specification
54. //==================================================================================================
55. //
56. // vstd does not provide a specification for `alloc::collections::LinkedList`. Verified functions in
57. // this module (`init`) take `LinkedList` parameters, so Verus needs to know the type. We declare it
58. // as an opaque external type. We deliberately do NOT provide a `View`/iterator specification: doing
59. // so requires implementing vstd's `View`/`ForLoopGhostIterator` traits for the foreign std types
60. // `LinkedList`/`Iter`, which the Rust orphan rule forbids from a downstream crate (E0117), and the
61. // pinned `vstd` dependency cannot be extended. Consequently the `for region in list.iter()` loops in
62. // `book_physical_memory_regions` / `book_mmio_regions` cannot be body-verified here; those two
63. // functions are marked `external_body` (see `verus-unsupported.md`).
64. 
65. verus! {
66. 
67. use core::alloc::Allocator;
68. 
69. #[verifier::external_type_specification]
70. #[verifier::external_body]
71. #[verifier::reject_recursive_types(T)]
72. #[verifier::reject_recursive_types(A)]
73. pub struct ExLinkedList<T, A: Allocator>(LinkedList<T, A>);
74. 
75. } // end verus!
76. 
77. //==================================================================================================
78. // `mm::phys` boot-subsystem View
79. //==================================================================================================
80. 
81. verus! {
82. 
83. use vstd::set_lib::set_int_range;
84. 
85. /// Abstract state of the global physical-memory subsystem managed by `mm::phys`.
86. ///
87. /// Models the boot lifecycle of the frame-allocator singleton plus its
88. /// frame-reservation state. The `frames` component mirrors `frame::instance()@`;
89. /// the `initialized` flag mirrors the `INSTANCE_INIT` lifecycle gate.
90. pub struct PhysMemView {
91.     /// Whether the frame-allocator singleton has been established
92.     /// (i.e. `init` ran once and returned `Ok`). Models one-shot/monotonic
93.     /// boot: `false` before `init`, `true` after a successful `init`.
94.     pub initialized: bool,
95.     /// Abstract reservation state of the global frame allocator: which physical
96.     /// frames are reserved (allocated) vs. free, with per-frame refcounts.
97.     /// Meaningful (well-formed) only once `initialized` is `true`.
98.     pub frames: FrameAllocView,
99. }
100. 
101. impl PhysMemView {
102.     /// Well-formedness: once the allocator is established, the frame-allocator
103.     /// invariant holds. Before initialization there is no allocator, so no
104.     /// constraint applies.
105.     pub open spec fn inv(self) -> bool {
106.         self.initialized ==> self.frames.wf()
107.     }
108. 
109.     /// Frames the allocator actually tracks (covered by the bitmap): the union
110.     /// of reserved and free frames. The abstract form of `is_covered`.
111.     pub open spec fn covered(self) -> Set<int> {
112.         self.frames.allocated_frames.union(self.frames.free_frames)
113.     }
114. 
115.     /// The set of frame addresses occupied by a region `[start, start+size)`.
116.     pub open spec fn region_frames(start: int, size: int) -> Set<int> {
117.         let first = start / spec_page_size();
118.         let last = (start + size) / spec_page_size();
119.         set_int_range(first, last).map(|i: int| i * spec_page_size())
120.     }
121. 
122.     /// `init` established the allocator from the caller-supplied bitmap state;
123.     /// lifecycle flips on.
124.     pub open spec fn spec_initialize(self, initial: FrameAllocView) -> PhysMemView {
125.         PhysMemView { initialized: true, frames: initial }
126.     }
127. 
128.     /// Book one covered frame: move `addr` from free to allocated, refcount = 1.
129.     /// Mirrors `Inner::book`'s `Ok` post-state.
130.     pub open spec fn spec_book_frame(self, addr: int) -> PhysMemView {
131.         PhysMemView {
132.             frames: FrameAllocView {
133.                 allocated_frames: self.frames.allocated_frames.insert(addr),
134.                 free_frames: self.frames.free_frames.remove(addr),
135.                 refcounts: self.frames.refcounts.insert(addr, 1int),
136.             },
137.             ..self
138.         }
139.     }
140. 
141.     /// Book a set of frames at once: move them all from free to allocated, each
142.     /// with refcount = 1. Mirrors `Inner::alloc_range`'s `Ok` post-state and
143.     /// generalizes it from a contiguous region to an arbitrary frame set.
144.     pub open spec fn spec_book_frames(self, frames: Set<int>) -> PhysMemView {
145.         PhysMemView {
146.             frames: FrameAllocView {
147.                 allocated_frames: self.frames.allocated_frames.union(frames),
148.                 free_frames: self.frames.free_frames.difference(frames),
149.                 refcounts: self.frames.refcounts.union_prefer_right(
150.                     Map::new(|a: int| frames.contains(a), |a: int| 1int),
151.                 ),
152.             },
153.             ..self
154.         }
155.     }
156. }
157. 
158. /// Abstract view of the global physical-memory subsystem at the current program
159. /// point.
160. ///
161. /// The subsystem state lives in module-level `static`s (`frame::INSTANCE` /
162. /// `frame::INSTANCE_INIT`) that a Verus `spec fn` cannot read directly, so this
163. /// is an *uninterpreted* function: the exec wrappers in `frame.rs` and the
164. /// `book_*`/`init` functions pin down its value through their `ensures` clauses.
165. /// `initialized` mirrors `INSTANCE_INIT`; `frames` mirrors `frame::instance()@`.
166. ///
167. /// This is the handle the caller-facing contract of `init` is stated over: after
168. /// a successful `init`, `phys_view().initialized` and `phys_view().inv()` hold, so
169. /// every later `frame::*` / `PhysMemoryManager::*` operation may rely on the
170. /// frame-allocator invariant.
171. pub uninterp spec fn phys_view() -> PhysMemView;
172. 
173. } // end verus!
174. 
175.

# TCB Allowed List — Nanvix phys-mm

Any `external_body` outside this list must be removed.

## Allowed `external_body`

- `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/mod.rs::book_physical_memory_regions` — iterates a std
  `alloc::collections::LinkedList` via `for region in list.iter()`. The build
  toolchain's `vstd` (`/mnt/toolchain/verus/vstd`) ships ghost-iterator specs only
  for `slice`/`vec`/`VecDeque`/`BTree*`/`Hash*` iterators, **not** `LinkedList`, and
  the orphan rule forbids supplying `View`/`ForLoopGhostIterator` impls for the
  foreign `linked_list::Iter` from the `kernel` crate (E0117). Genuine Verus
  front-end limitation, not a proof gap or code bug — full analysis in
  `verus-unsupported.md`. The abstract booking effect is specified over
  `PhysMemView` and discharged (no `admit`) by
  `lemma_book_region_reserves_region_frames` in `mod.proof.rs`. `ensures` keeps the
  caller-relevant guarantee: allocator stays initialized and well-formed.
- `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/mod.rs::book_mmio_regions` — same std-`LinkedList`
  iteration limitation as above. Abstract effect (skip-if-not-covered; book tracked
  frames) discharged by `lemma_book_mmio_skip_untracked` /
  `lemma_book_mmio_books_tracked`. `ensures` keeps allocator initialized and
  well-formed across booking.
- `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/kframe.rs::KernelFrame::deref`
- `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/kframe.rs::KernelFrame::deref_mut`
- `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/kframe.rs::KernelFrame::clear`
- `src/libs/bump_allocator/src/lib.rs::FixedSizeBumpAllocator::alloc` — materializes a
  `&'static mut [u8; N]` from a backend-provided address (`usize as *mut`); raw-memory
  op Verus cannot verify without a `PointsTo` for the externally-owned `BssStorage`
  region. Mirrors `src/libs/raw-array`. `ensures` states alignment + in-bounds over
  the abstract `bump_view`.
- `src/libs/bump_allocator/src/lib.rs::FixedSizeBumpAllocator::alloc_as` — delegates to
  `alloc` and re-materializes the slot as `&'static mut MaybeUninit<T>`; same rationale.
  `ensures` adds the `size_of::<T>()`/`align_of::<T>()` vs `(N, A)` guard arms.

## Skip / exclude from current proof target

- `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/manager.rs::PhysMemoryManager::get_mut`
- `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/frame.rs::init`
